# AF 第三章 原文（重制基线）

## Chapter 3

[P01] How they toiled（苦干） and sweated（出汗了） to get the hay（干草） in! But their efforts were rewarded, for the harvest was even bigger than they had hoped. Sometimes the work was hard; the tools had been made for human beings, not for animals, and no animal could use any tool that involved（卷入） standing on his hind（后面的） legs. But the pigs were so clever that they could think of a way round every difficulty. As for the horses, they knew every inch of the field, and understood mowing（割草） and raking（耙草） far better than Jones and his men had ever done.

[P02] The pigs did not work, but led and checked the others. With their greater knowledge, they took the lead. Boxer and Clover put on the harness（马具） and pulled the cutter（切割机） or the horse-rake（耙子） (no bits or reins（缰绳） were needed) and walked steadily（稳定地） round the field with a pig behind calling out "Gee（驾） up, comrade（同志）!" or "Whoa（停） back, comrade!" as needed. And every animal, even the lowliest（最卑微）, worked at turning the hay and gathering（聚集） it. Even the ducks and hens toiled all day in the sun, carrying tiny wisps（小捆） of hay in their beaks（鸟嘴）.

[P03] In the end they finished the harvest two days faster than Jones and his men usually did. Moreover, it was the biggest harvest the farm had ever seen. Nothing was wasted; the hens and ducks had picked up the very last stalk（茎）. And no animal had stolen even a mouthful（一口）. It was a drawback（缺点） that no animal could use any tool on his hind legs. But they found a way round every difficulty. The pigs supervised（监督） and took the lead. The horses pulled the cutter and the rake and walked steadily round the field, while a pig called out "Gee up, comrade!" or "Whoa back, comrade!" All through that summer the work of the farm went like clockwork（钟表）.

[P04] The animals were happy as they had never imagined possible. Every mouthful of food was a real pleasure, now that it was truly their own food, made by themselves and for themselves, not handed out by a grudging（勉强） master. With the parasitic（寄生） humans gone, there was more for everyone to eat. There was more rest too. They met with many troubles—for instance（例子）, later in the year, when they harvested the corn, they had to tread（踩） it out in the old way and blow away the chaff（谷壳） with their breath, since the farm had no threshing（打谷） machine—but the pigs with their cleverness（聪明） and Boxer with his tremendous（极大的） muscles（肌肉） always pulled them through.

[P05] Boxer was the admiration（钦佩） of everybody. He had been a hard worker even in Jones's time, but now he seemed more like three horses than one; there were days when the whole work of the farm seemed to rest on his mighty（强大） shoulders. From morning to night he was pushing and pulling, always at the spot（地点） where the work was hardest. He had made an arrangement（安排） with one of the cockerels（小公鸡） to call him in the mornings half an hour earlier than anyone else, and would put in some volunteer labour（劳作） at whatever seemed to be most needed, before the regular day's work began. His answer to every problem, every setback（挫折）, was "I will work harder!"--which he had adopted（采用） as his personal motto. But everyone worked according to his capacity（能力）.

[P06] The hens and ducks, for instance, saved five bushels（蒲式耳） of corn at the harvest by gathering up the stray（走失） grains（谷物）. Nobody stole, nobody grumbled（抱怨） over his rations（配给）, the quarrelling（争吵） and biting and jealousy（嫉妒） which had been normal in the old days had almost disappeared. Nobody shirked（偷懒）--or almost nobody. Mollie, it was true, was not good at getting up in the mornings, and had a way of leaving work early, saying there was a stone（石头） in her hoof（蹄）. The cat was also peculiar（奇怪）: when there was work to be done, it could never be found.

[P07] She would disappear for hours, then come back at meal-times, or in the evening after work, as if nothing had happened. But her excuses were so good, and she purred（咕噜叫） so warmly, that nobody could doubt her kind intentions（意图）. Old Benjamin, the donkey, seemed just the same since the uprising（起义）. He worked in the same slow, stubborn（固执） way as in Jones's time, never shirking（逃避） and never asking for extra（额外） work. About the uprising and what came of it, he said nothing. Asked if he was not happier now that Jones was gone, he would say only, "Donkeys live a long time.

[P08] None of you has ever seen a dead donkey," and the others had to be content（满足） with this cryptic（神秘） answer. He would say only, "Donkeys live a long time. None of you has ever seen a dead donkey," On Sundays the others had to be content with this cryptic answer. On Sundays there was no work. Breakfast was an hour later than usual, and after breakfast there was a ceremony which took place every week without fail. First came the raising of the flag. Snowball had found in the harness-room an old green tablecloth（桌布） of Mrs. Jones's and had painted on it a hoof and a horn in white.

[P09] This was run up the flagstaff（旗杆） in the farmhouse（农舍） garden every Sunday morning. The flag was green, Snowball explained, to stand for the green fields of England, while the hoof and horn meant the future Republic（共和国） of the Animals which would come when the human race was finally overthrown（推翻）. After the hoisting（升起） of the flag all the animals trooped（成群） into the big barn（谷仓） for a general assembly（集会） known as the Meeting. Here the work of the coming week was planned out and resolutions were put forward and debated. It was always the pigs who put forward the resolutions. The other animals understood how to vote, but could never think of any resolutions of their own.

[P10] Snowball and Napoleon were by far the most active in the debates. But it was noticed that these two were never in agreement: whatever suggestion either of them made, the other could be counted on to oppose（反对） it. Even when it was resolved（决心）--a thing no one could object to in itself--to set aside（旁边） the small paddock（围场） behind the orchard（果园） as a home of rest for animals who were past work, there was a stormy（暴风雨） debate over the correct retiring（退休） age for each class of animal. The Meeting always ended with the singing of 'animals of England', and the afternoon was given up to recreation（娱乐）.

[P11] Here, in the evenings, they studied blacksmithing（打铁）, carpentering（木工活）, and other necessary arts from books brought out of the farmhouse. Snowball also organised the other animals into Animal Committees（委员会）. He was tireless（不知疲倦）. He formed the Egg Production Committee（委员会） for the hens, the Clean Tails League（联盟） for the cows, the Wild Comrades（同志们）' Re-education Committee (to tame（驯服） the rats and rabbits), the Whiter Wool（羊毛） Movement for the sheep, and others, besides classes in reading and writing. On the whole, these projects failed. The attempt（尝试） to tame the wild creatures（生物）, for instance, broke down at once.

[P12] They went on behaving just as before, and when treated with generosity（慷慨）, simply took advantage of it. The cat joined the Re-education Committee and was active for a few days. One day she was seen on a roof, talking to some sparrows（麻雀） just out of her reach. She told them all animals were now comrades and any sparrow（麻雀） could come and perch on her paw（爪子）; but the sparrows kept their distance. The reading and writing classes were a great success. By the autumn almost every animal could read and write in some degree. As for the pigs, they could already read and write perfectly.

[P13] The dogs learned to read fairly well, but cared for nothing except the Seven Commandments（戒律）. Muriel, the goat, could read a little better than the dogs, and sometimes read to the others in the evenings from bits of newspaper she found on the rubbish heap（堆）. Benjamin could read as well as any pig, but never used his skill. As far as he knew, he said, there was nothing worth reading. Clover learnt the whole alphabet（字母表）, but could not put words together. Boxer could not get past the letter D. He would trace（痕迹） out A, B, C, D, in the dust（灰尘） with his great hoof, and then stand staring at the letters with his ears back, trying with all his might to remember what came next and never succeeding.

[P14] On several occasions, indeed, he did learn E, F, G, H, but by the time he knew them, it was always found that he had forgotten A, B, C, and D. Finally he decided to be happy with the first four letters, and used to write them out once or twice every day to refresh（恢复） his memory. Mollie refused to learn any but the six letters which spelt（拼写） her own name. She would form these very neatly out of pieces of twig, and would then decorate them with a flower or two and walk round them admiring them, using scrap scraps of newspaper from the rubbish heap.

[P15] It was also found that the stupider animals, such as the sheep, hens, and ducks, could not learn the Seven Commandments by heart. After much thought Snowball declared（宣布） that the Seven Commandments could in effect be reduced to a single maxim（格言）: "Four legs good, two legs bad." This, he said, contained the essential（必要） principle（原则） of Animalism（动物主义）. Whoever（任何人） had fully grasped（掌握） it would be safe from human influences. The birds at first objected, since it seemed that they also had two legs, but Snowball proved that this was not so. "A bird's wing, comrades," he said, "is an organ（器官） of propulsion（推进） and not of manipulation（操作）."

[P16] It should therefore be regarded as a leg. The mark that makes man different is the HAND, the tool for all his bad deeds（事迹）." The birds did not understand Snowball's long words, but accepted his explanation, and the humbler（更卑微） animals set to work to learn the new maxim by heart. FOUR LEGS GOOD, TWO LEGS BAD, was written on the end wall of the barn, above the Seven Commandments and in bigger letters. Once they had learned it, the sheep liked this maxim, and often as they lay in the field they would all start bleating "Four legs good, two legs bad!"

[P17] "Four legs good, two legs bad!" and keep it up for hours on end, never getting tired of it. Long words such as "Bleat Napoleon" took no interest in Snowball's committees. He said that the education of the young was more important than anything that could be done for those who were already grown up. It happened that Jessie and Bluebell had both whelped（下崽） soon after the hay harvest, giving birth between them to nine sturdy（强壮） puppies. As soon as they were weaned（断奶）, Napoleon took them away from their mothers, saying that he would make himself responsible for their education. He took them up into a loft（阁楼） which could only be reached by a ladder from the harness-room, and there kept them in such seclusion（隐居） that the rest of the farm soon forgot they existed（存在）.

[P18] It was mixed every day into the pigs' mash（糊状饲料）. The early apples were now ripening（成熟）, and the grass of the orchard was covered with windfalls（落果）. The animals had thought, as a matter of course, that these would be shared out equally; one day, however, the order came that all the windfalls were to be collected and brought to the harness-room for the pigs to use. At this some of the other animals murmured（低语）, but it was no use. All the pigs agreed fully on this point, even Snowball and Napoleon. Squealer was sent to explain it to the others. "Comrades!" he cried.

[P19] "You do not imagine, I hope, that we pigs are doing this out of selfishness（自私） and privilege（特权）? Many of us actually dislike（不喜欢） milk and apples. I dislike them myself. Our only aim in taking these things is to keep our health. Milk and apples, comrades, contain things absolutely（绝对） necessary to the well-being of a pig. We pigs are brainworkers（脑力劳动者）. The whole management（管理） of this farm depends on us. Day and night we watch over your welfare（福利）. It is for YOUR sake（利益） that we drink that milk and eat those apples. Do you know what would happen if we pigs failed in our duty?

[P20] Jones would come back! Yes, Jones would come back! Surely, comrades," cried Squealer almost pleadingly（恳求地）, jumping from side to side and whisking（搅拌） his tail, "surely no one among you wants to see Jones come back?" If there was one thing the animals were certain of, it was that they did not want Jones back. Put in this light, they had no more to say. The importance of keeping the pigs healthy was too clear. So it was agreed without further（进一步） argument（争论） that the milk and the windfall（落果） apples (and the main crop when they ripened（成熟）) should be kept for the pigs alone.
